notes: Paths are relative to the data root (AIC_DATA_DIR, default ./data).
'required' strings are the pass/fail gate: every one must appear in the engine output.
'required_phrases' must survive reading-order reconstruction, not just line detection.
'full_text' is a best-effort reference transcription used for CER and word recall only.

'unreadable' lists text that is on the frame and in 'full_text' but has been demonstrated unreadable — not merely missed by the current engine. It is deleted from both reference and hypothesis before CER and word recall, so excluding it can neither reward nor punish an engine. Every entry must cite its evidence in 'comment'.

'ignore_regions' are normalised (x0,y0,x1,y1) boxes of burned-in station furniture — channel logos and on-screen clocks. Lines centred inside them are dropped before scoring, and are absent from 'full_text', because scripts.ocr.postprocess.suppress_static_overlays removes them before indexing: scoring them would measure text no query can ever reach.
Frames with acceptance=true are the user-specified acceptance criteria and are hand-labelled.

frames.comment: Flood-depth gauge on a pillar. Digits alternate left/right in a checkerboard, ~15px tall in a narrow vertical strip, on a low-contrast pink/white pattern. Default 960px detection resize erases them entirely. Masked: the HTV9 bug and clock top-right, and the scrolling news crawl along the bottom. The crawl is excluded on instruction — queries ask about text belonging to the scene, not about unrelated headlines running under a broadcast — which leaves this frame testing exactly one thing, which is what it was chosen for. The crawl mask starts at 0.90 rather than 0.87: the lowest gauge digit's centre sits at 0.889 and a taller band swallows it.

frames.comment: Requested as K17_V003 frame 11187, which has no keyframe; 11191 is the nearest, 4 frames away. A tourism signboard: red block caps followed by the place name in a green brush script, over a wall-mounted map. The scrolling crawl and the station bug are masked, so what remains is scene text of exactly the kind competition queries ask about. The signboard is the hard part: the detector merges the red caps and the script into one box, so VietOCR returns 'KHU DU LỊCH QUỐC GIAMMECCHING', and reading the script in isolation gives 'MACHY' at 0.44 confidence, below the floor. Only a vision-LLM shown the whole frame recovers 'Mộc Châu' -- and magnifying the script for it makes things worse, not better (4x drops the tone marks, 8x gives 'Mac Clean'), because the model is reading context as much as pixels. Lowering det_unclip_ratio to split the merged box was measured at 1.4/1.6/2.0 and never separates them while costing 0.964 -> 0.875 required recall on the other frames, so 1.8 stands. The map labels HOÀNG SA / TRƯỜNG SA carry the 'unreadable' exclusion: ~45x8px teal-on-white over a cluttered ball mosaic, undetectable at 4x, 6x, 8x and 12x magnification of their own ROI, so this is below the detector's floor rather than a tuning failure.

frames.full_text: PHÚ XUÂN - GIA ĐỊNH NHỮNG DẤU ẤN LỊCH SỬ
frames.comment: Found by visual search while answering a competition-style temporal query, so it is genuinely held out: nothing about the engine was tuned on it. It earns its place because the two sources of the leading configuration each get exactly half of it right, which four frames of tuning had hidden. The Qwen2.5-VL corrector reads 'GIA ĐỊNH' correctly and 'DẤU ẤN' as 'ĐẦU ÂN'; the Qwen3-VL-8B spine does the reverse, 'GIA ĐÌNH' and 'DẤU ẤN'. A two-source merge must therefore guess, and guesses wrong half the time, while adding any third voter resolves both by majority. Verified at 3x magnification: the board reads PHÚ XUÂN - GIA ĐỊNH / NHỮNG DẤU ẤN LỊCH SỬ. The decorative face places a dot between letters (P·HÚ, N·H·H), which is what the models trip on. Masked: the HTV9 bug with its clock, and the bottom news crawl. Note this is a K video, and indexes/profiles/ covers only the L videos, so app.py would currently drop a hit here entirely.
